Research & publications — Bingkun Qi

Selected research and publications on non-Hermitian photonics, parity–time symmetry and photonic zero modes.

A question to enter the research

Featured publication · Why does light form steps near the edge of a lattice?

When light fades away from a defect, does the brightness ratio between neighboring sites have to change too?

A single intensity image reveals two distinct properties: the contrast within a pair of sites and the decay across many pairs.

In a lattice with alternating gain and loss, non-Hermitian particle–hole symmetry allows an entire band of modes to share one oscillation frequency when the gain and loss are sufficiently strong. At fixed edge detuning, changing gain and loss alters how fast the defect mode fades across the array while preserving the intensity ratio within each unit cell.

Bingkun Qi is the first author.

Read the source

Anchoring a zero mode at the boundary

Can a mode retain its reference frequency without global symmetry?

This suggests another route to frequency-stable photonic devices.

Coupling a boundary zero mode to the bulk under specific non-Hermitian conditions yields a zero mode robust to bulk disorder. The boundary and coupling conditions must remain satisfied.

Bingkun Qi is a co-author, listed third.

Physical Review Letters 120, 093901 · 2018

Defect States Emerging from a Non-Hermitian Flatband of Photonic Zero Modes

Bingkun Qi, Lingxuan Zhang, Li Ge

In a lattice with alternating gain and loss, non-Hermitian particle–hole symmetry allows an entire band of modes to share one oscillation frequency when the gain and loss are sufficiently strong. At fixed edge detuning, changing gain and loss alters how fast the defect mode fades across the array while preserving the intensity ratio within each unit cell.

First author
